title: A multinational in a host country: case and evaluate frame
subject: Business
unit: Spring 1: The international economy and government (1.5, 1.6)
source: Written for business/y10 lesson 27 (Pupil PDF worksheet: host-country case and evaluate frame)
intro: Lesson 27. Read the case, then evaluate the statement.

passage.title: A car-parts factory near Tangier, Morocco
paras: Atlas Components, a European multinational that makes car parts, has opened a factory near the port of Tangier in Morocco. It chose Morocco because wages are lower than in Europe, the port is close to its customers' car plants, and Morocco has trade agreements with the European Union, so its parts are sold there without tariffs.

The factory employs 1,200 local people. Wages are about 15% above the local average and every worker gets six weeks of training. The government gave the company a five-year break from some taxes to attract it.

Most of the profit is sent back to the company's head office in Europe. Two small local workshops say they have lost skilled staff to the factory. Farmers nearby are worried about the amount of water the factory uses.
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

blocks.h: Answer frame (6 marks: both sides, then a supported judgement)

blocks.text: 'A multinational opening a factory is always good for the host country.' Evaluate this statement. (6 marks)

frame.label: For: point and chain of reasoning in context
Against: point and chain of reasoning in context
Judgement
frame.prompt: Decide, give the main reason, and say what it depends on.

markScheme.a: For: 1,200 jobs at wages 15% above average and training raise skills and incomes; spending in the local economy. Against: profits leave the country; a tax break means less tax for the government at first; local workshops lose staff; water use harms farmers. Judgement: 'not always'; it depends on whether the government makes rules on wages, water and local suppliers, and on how long the factory stays.
